# Imajin

> identity and authority for AI agents.

your agents act as themselves, on your authority, and every action is signed.

Imajin is alpha. [Book a demo or join as a tester, integrator or partner](https://imajin.ai/alpha); this is not self-serve onboarding.

Point your agent at it: use your runtime with the Imajin plugin and kernel to establish identity, delegated authority and a signed record. Every action is a signed event that anyone can verify, including a third party's own agent. Cost and credit are recorded per identity, and .fair turns that into who gets paid.

## What Imajin is

The kernel serves **Attestation · Communication · Attribution · Settlement · Discovery · Revocation**, plus shared rails. Identity is their subject, not another primitive. Apps built on Imajin register separate identities and integrate through scoped public APIs, not kernel imports or another service's tables. Broker-agent and corpus are internal services.

Imajin is source-available under the [Imajin Network License](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/LICENSE.md). Source support and service specs are not deployment evidence or permission grants.

## Key concepts

Imajin records proof of history, not proof that a statement is true. Actor-key signatures, node-witnessed actions and unsigned logs have different evidentiary strength. Revocation withdraws current authority while retaining tombstones and provenance, not deleting signed history.

- **Identity:** People, agents and groups have distinct DIDs. Key-backed identities use Ed25519; soft identities have no actor signing key. Standing tiers are soft, preliminary, established, steward and operator, not blanket permission.
- **Acting identity:** Human `x-acting-as` organization context requires live membership, role and allowed services. A refusal never falls back to the personal DID. An agent proves its own identity; assignment does not itself grant a capability.
- **Agent handles:** Create and Provision use the stored acting owner's `@<owner>-jin` prefix with an optional suffix. Leave the UI suffix blank for the base; APIs send the full handle. Collisions return 409 rather than random renaming; owners without handles supply an explicit full handle. Existing agents keep their handles.
- **Attribution and settlement:** A .fair manifest describes credit and economic distribution, not proof of payment. Fees and signature verification depend on the flow. MJN is receipt-backed and withdrawable subject to rail rules; emitted MJNx is not withdrawable, and the ledger does not silently convert units.
- **Connectors:** Vendor, purpose (`inference` or `billing`), holder DID and slot are independent. Provider spelling grants no authority. Human member grants and an agent's verified principal relationship are separate; apps receive authorized operations, not provider keys.
- **Custody:** Node-sealed and delegation-grant entries coexist. Tier 0 remains node-controlled, not zero-custody. Organization keys are write-only, including for the loading admin; metadata is not credential release.

### Identity, disclosure and proof

Key-backed registration derives a `did:imajin:` identifier from base58 public-key bytes and verifies Ed25519 proof. DFOS linking is separate and optional. Soft identity resolution is not verified onboarding or a browser session. Use verified effective identity for ownership, names, handles and labels, not the raw controller DID.

Agent handles are validated against the stored serving principal. Entering the whole prefix in a suffix field or an invalid full handle is refused; there is no name-derived random fallback. A selected owner cannot grant authority by changing a label. Organization provisioning and orphan adoption retain their own human-admin and proof requirements.

An attestation's documented signer and payload determine what it proves. Node-witnessed records are not device-key countersignatures. Private legal-entity fields and sealed bank identifiers use dedicated disclosure helpers; generic media or vault permissions cannot disclose them. Replacement and revocation preserve signed history.

Operator approval authorizes its specific operation or ceiling, not user consent or an agent's grant. Long-running work must tolerate expiry and revocation. Signed loop events, decisions and outcomes are principal-scoped; a transport acknowledgement proves attempted delivery, not completed work or an acquired lease. Private briefs and artifacts retain their access controls. Consult the Jin spec and loop contracts rather than treating harness-local references as public capabilities.

### Settlement and ledger units

Creative attribution and payment shares are different fields. Use shared manifest builders and the owning pay contract rather than copying a fee chain. Protocol, platform, node, buyer, tax, scope and processor handling depend on the flow; there is no universal two-percent fee or blanket unsigned-manifest rejection. A payment receipt and recorded settlement outcome, not a manifest alone, establish payment.

MJN follows receipt currency and withdrawal rules. MJNx is emitted for in-platform use. Accepted-unit checks reject unsupported units, without automatic conversion, a fixed fiat peg or a token-launch guarantee.

### Connectors, delegation and custody

Registration, operator approval, member consent and agent delegation are independent gates. Organization key lifecycle requires live human owner/admin act-as with connections-service authority. Human members require an active member grant; assigned agents use verified principal relationships and live allowed-service and revocation checks.

The registry separates vendor from purpose and holder. Billing credentials do not authorize inference, or vice versa. App upstreams retain the member-approved declaration binding independently of their vendor hostname; names or metadata cannot substitute for that binding. Suspensions survive reconnecting and retagging, and rejoining does not restore revoked member grants.

Member-held Postman access permits reviewed saved-data reads at the fixed official target, not arbitrary writes or live request execution. App-hosted upstreams declare exact destinations and method/path ceilings. Permission-set changes require reconnection. Writes need distinct scope and a reason; redirects and credential echoes are refused. Credentials stay in the kernel; no DB transaction spans upstream network I/O. Successful calls and admitted upstream failures retain signed outcome metadata, while admission refusals do not write permanent outcomes.

Vault node-sealed and delegation-grant custody have different limits. Optional external-owner custody is not a universal deployment posture. Seal credentials only through documented controls, never source, chat, commands or logs.

### Communication and security limits

Chat uses TLS in transit and stores plaintext at rest on the hosting node in `chat.messages_v2.content`. Push notifications carry the first 200 characters of the message preview. Message encryption is planned but not implemented; public key bundles do not protect current messages. No forward-secrecy or post-compromise guarantee is made. WebSocket transport shares the kernel HTTP server; that does not hide stored content from the host.

## How to integrate

### Connect an agent

Give the agent its own DID and signing key through the [auth contract](https://jin.imajin.ai/auth/api/spec). A person grants scoped delegation for the capabilities and audience it needs, with expiry and revocation. Keep the agent signer distinct from the principal it serves.

Use the kernel's [MCP server](https://mcp.imajin.ai/mcp), served at `/mcp`, with protected-resource/OAuth discovery, authorization code, PKCE and explicit consent. Each agent needs its own client and credential/refresh store. A consent-bound agent/principal pair cannot be switched by a request header; new principals or wider scopes need fresh consent. Tokens are resource-bound and scopes are only a ceiling; tools still enforce live authority.

For contacting one person, use their `/reach/<handle>/mcp` and `/reach/<handle>/openapi.json` on the node. Public discovery is not contact permission: gated calls need recipient-bound authority. A reach bearer is not a general kernel token or authority to act as the recipient.

The [OpenClaw plugin](https://github.com/ima-jin/openclaw-imajin-plugin) is the working integration example. Follow the [MCP runbook](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/ops/openclaw-mcp.md) for consent and principal isolation; retain the plugin's documented direct identity, attestation and inbound-message paths where MCP is not equivalent.

### Build an app

Start with the [registered-app contract](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/REGISTRATION.md) and [app template](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-app-template). Use published `@ima-jin/*` SDKs externally; `@imajin/*` is the workspace scope, and `private: true` is not publication evidence.

Begin sign-in in the app's own handler, preserve isolated callback state and exchange the short-lived single-use code with proof of the app's signing key. Trust the kernel-returned subject, not client profile fields. Keep app cookies isolated from the kernel and other apps. The [auth-client README](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/packages/auth-client/README.md) owns the SDK contract.

Use user-delegated tokens for consented user operations and operator-approved app-service tokens only for their documented machine operations. Neither substitutes for a human session where required. Manifest secret sync creates slots only: signed Generate or masked Set plus countersignature activates approved material. Load vault credentials into typed server-only memory before DB/server imports, never into client bundles or `process.env`.

### Discover models and connector authority

`GET /infer/v1/self` returns the agent's identity, usable models, inference routes, authority, grant status and fixing controls. Read-only MCP/HTTP rows reuse tool-call authorization predicates, including `authorizedScopes`, without probing credentials. Inference scope is not tool authority. The `?agents=1` operator view backs serving-agent cards on `/jin` and requires a direct authorized principal session; it does not expose agents' private connectors.

Use the calling agent's refreshed credential with the [passthrough](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/packages/openclaw-infer-passthrough/README.md). A configured selector never grants access to another identity's key; there is no agent-mode shared, personal or direct-provider fallback after refusal. Billing reconciliation uses a separate sealed credential and billing scope; incurred usage is not a complete provider invoice, and missing cost is not evidence of free use.

### Clone or fetch GitHub repositories

Use the agent-mode loopback passthrough and the owner's active primary GitHub connector plus live `github:read` delegation. Only the kernel contacts GitHub with the owner's sealed credential. Push is refused; host-static mode does not serve git and there is no proxy mint, GitHub login or direct fallback.

Supply the fresh Imajin Bearer only through process memory/environment, never persistent git configuration. Multiple eligible owners require `X-Acting-For`; it narrows granted authority and cannot override a consent-bound owner. Do not send inference's `x-acting-as` header on the agent git lane. Grants and connector authority are rechecked per protocol request. Revocation denies the next request, not bytes already transferred.

The node-signed `github.git.fetch` record describes a requested operation, not successful transfer. Per-grant repository allowlists are not implemented: the selected credential's readable repositories bound access. Follow the [git-read runbook](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/agents/github-git-read-proxy.md) for configuration, refusal behavior and private-repository verification; the GitHub service spec currently describes OAuth/connection operations, not this transport.

### Run a node

Use [contributor setup](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPER.md), [environments](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md) and [deployment](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/deploy/README.md). The kernel has no basePath; independently owned apps own theirs. Kernel-owned liveness uses a bounded shared-pool query. Independent listeners opt in with ecosystem `LIVENESS_PATH`; an undeclared app is not an HTTP-watchdog target.

Corpus is an internal daemon with a private configured service address and its own `/spec`. GitHub partitions require registry-resolved source-owner groups and explicit owner grants; membership, stubs and a local CLI login are not authority. Follow the [corpus runbook](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/apps/corpus/README.md).

## Service specifications

These links derive from checked-in service definitions and their spec handlers, not deployment inventory or permission. Substitute your node's origin. Specs are the route catalogue, not this guide. The git transport's dedicated runbook supplements the GitHub OAuth spec.

- [Auth API](https://jin.imajin.ai/auth/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Calendar API](https://jin.imajin.ai/calendar/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Chat API](https://jin.imajin.ai/chat/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Cloudflare API](https://jin.imajin.ai/cloudflare/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Connections API](https://jin.imajin.ai/connections/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [GitHub API](https://jin.imajin.ai/github/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Google API](https://jin.imajin.ai/google/api/spec): Not publicly served at this origin; no public spec handler is defined. Consult the [contract source](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/apps/kernel/api-spec/google.yaml).
- [Infer API](https://jin.imajin.ai/infer/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Jin API](https://jin.imajin.ai/jin/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Media API](https://jin.imajin.ai/media/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Notify API](https://jin.imajin.ai/notify/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Pay API](https://jin.imajin.ai/pay/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Profile API](https://jin.imajin.ai/profile/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [QuickBooks API](https://jin.imajin.ai/quickbooks/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Registry API](https://jin.imajin.ai/registry/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Usage API](https://jin.imajin.ai/usage/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.
- [Vault API](https://jin.imajin.ai/vault/api/spec): Service-owned schemas, authentication and errors.

Corpus has a [service-owned runbook and private spec source](https://github.com/ima-jin/imajin-ai/blob/main/apps/corpus/README.md); do not assume a public kernel path.
